title: From prosthetic memory to prosthetic denial: Auditing whether large language models are prone to mass atrocity denialism
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the accuracy and susceptibility to denialist framings of LLM responses concerning four historical mass atrocities. The primary connection to religion is through the case study of the Holocaust, which involved questions about the genocide against the Jewish people.
findings: While models generally performed well on questions about the Holocaust, they still produced factual inaccuracies (e.g., regarding victim counts at Majdanek), inconsistencies, and exhibited language-specific issues. For instance, models struggled with the German-language nuances of the term 'genocide' when applied to the killing of Jews, disagreeing with the term in German while agreeing in English. The paper concludes that even infrequent errors are significant given the sensitive nature of the topic.
